description.narrative: The Xochimilco and San Gregorio Atlapulco natural protected area (ANP) is home of a unique pre-Hispanic agro-ecological system consisting of biodiversity-rich chinampas (floating gardens) and channels that host a variety of endemic species such as Ambystoma mexicanum. In addition, the area is an important water reservoir for the entire population of Mexico City. In the last 60 years the system has undergone serious changes in its hydrological regime and food web due to domestic sewage discharges and chemical fertilizers and pesticide run off. Through this project, REDES plans to implement an intensive hands-on training program for young local residents and users of the ANP focused on environmental education, sustainable agricultural production techniques, ecosystem management and restoration techniques, invasive species control, climate change, native species conservation, among others. A total of 75 sessions of 3.5 hours each will be taught, including field practices. The second part of the project includes the implementation of individual restoration projects in the chinampas of each one of the program participants. The third and final part of this project consists of a public outreach program aimed at the general public. The purpose of this activity is to create an open discussion forum where participants develop the solutions to the environmental problems faced in the area that can be turned into concrete conservation actions.
